schema.title: Response List Platforms Api Platforms Get

post.description:
Verify credentials, set session cookies, and return the login body.

401 (generic) on any mismatch.

Public self-registration. Always creates a REQUESTER and auto-logs in.

The role is forced — the client cannot escalate to admin here (only
``POST /api/users`` can, and that is admin-gated). 403 when open
registration is disabled; 409 on a duplicate username; throttled per
(ip, username) like login. Returns a JWT so the UI logs in immediately.

Rotate the session from the refresh cookie: issue a new access + refresh
pair (rotation) and re-set both cookies. 401 if the refresh cookie is
missing/invalid/expired or the user is gone.

Clear the session cookies. (Tokens are stateless, so this is the session
end for cookie clients; Bearer clients simply drop their token.)

schema.title: Response List Users Api Users Get

post.description: Create a user with a hashed password (admin only). 409 on duplicate name.
Live credential probe. Does NOT persist anything.
Discovery preview for the wizard. Does NOT persist anything.

Atomic onboard: re-discover, then persist device + ports + backup + audit.

Discovery runs BEFORE the transaction — if it fails, there is no DB hit.
The persist runs inside one ``session.begin()`` block; any failure rolls
the whole unit back, leaving no orphan device or ports.

get.description: List devices (optional ``?environment=<site slug>`` filter). Never returns creds.

schema.title: Response List Devices Api Devices Get

delete.description:
Offboard a device.

port_metadata + backups cascade via FK ondelete=CASCADE (operational data).
Change-request history uses FK ondelete=RESTRICT, so a device that has any
change requests CANNOT be hard-deleted — the compliance trail must be
retained. That case surfaces as 409 Conflict rather than an unhandled 500.

patch.description:
Re-test new creds against the device; only store them if the probe passes.

On a failed probe the stored (old) credentials are left untouched — 400.

Enable/disable config writes for a device (gradual rollout / kill-switch).

Does NOT override intrinsic read-only status (router/vpn role or a
non-writable platform) — ``writable`` in the response reflects the combined
policy. Audited.

post.description:
Re-probe an onboarded device and refresh its stored snapshot.

Non-destructive: adds metadata rows only for ports seen for the first time
(human edits preserved) and writes a fresh baseline backup. 502 on a probe
failure. Invalidates the live port-state cache so the next read is fresh.

get.description: List every site in the catalog, with live device counts.

schema.title: Response List Sites Api Sites Get

post.description: Create a new site (admin only). Slug must be unique.

patch.description: Rename a site (admin only). The slug is immutable to keep URLs stable.

delete.description: Delete a site (admin only). Blocked if any device is still assigned.

get.description: Live port list (cached 30s). ``?refresh=true`` bypasses the cache.

schema.title: Response Get Ports Api Devices  Device Id  Ports Get

get.description: Single-port detail: live state + metadata + recent audit history.

patch.description:
Admin direct edit of port *metadata* (host_model/bmc_ip/notes).

Metadata-only: this writes the DB ``port_metadata`` row, NOT the device, so
``assert_writable`` is deliberately not invoked. Writes an audit entry and
stamps ``last_human_edit_*``.

Admin-only DIRECT write of the on-device port description.

Declared BEFORE the metadata ``:path`` route so ``…/description`` matches
here, not as a port named ``…/description``.

schema.title: Response Set Port Description Api Devices  Device Id  Ports  Port Name  Description Patch

patch.description:
Admin-only DIRECT write of device port tunables.

Covers port-mode (access/trunk), native/untagged VLAN, tagged VLANs, MTU and
admin enable/disable. Declared BEFORE the metadata ``:path`` route. Immediate
commit, no approval gate; 403 for non-admin, 422 if no field is set.

schema.title: Response Set Port Config Api Devices  Device Id  Ports  Port Name  Config Patch

get.description: Running config (cached). ``?refresh=true`` re-fetches from the device.

Live system snapshot: control-plane protocols, mgmt services, MAC table.

Sections a driver can't reach come back empty (``mac_supported=false``
distinguishes an unreadable MAC table from a genuinely empty one).

Operational detail (named tables) for one protocol — e.g. OSPF neighbors
+ link-state database. Parsed from device CLI gets via TextFSM.

The device's VLAN database: id, name, description, L3 SVI, member-port
count. Backs the VLANs view and the request VLAN picker.

schema.title: Response Get Vlans Api Devices  Device Id  Vlans Get

get.description: Addressed/non-switchport interfaces: management port, L3 VLAN SVIs, LAGs.

schema.title: Response Get L3 Interfaces Api Devices  Device Id  L3 Interfaces Get

post.description: Take a config backup now (admin).

get.description: List a device's config backups, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Backups Api Devices  Device Id  Config Backups Get

get.description: Unified diff of a stored backup vs the current running config.

post.description: File a change request. 403 if the target device is read-only (fail fast).

get.description:
List requests.

Non-admin callers ALWAYS see only their own requests — the client ``?mine``
flag is ignored for them so it cannot be used to enumerate others' requests.
Admins see every request and may narrow with ``?mine`` / ``?request_status``.

schema.title: Response List Requests Api Requests Get

post.description: File a VLAN-database change request (create/delete a VLAN). 403 if read-only.
File a VRF create/delete request. 403 if the device is read-only.

File a routed-interface change request (SVI / loopback). 403 if read-only.

422 if the L3 intent is internally inconsistent (e.g. svi without vlan_id,
create without ipv4) — validated by the L3Change model.

get.description:
Request detail, including the rendered diff if available.

Non-admin callers may only read their own request; a foreign id returns 404
(object-level authz — see :func:`_assert_can_read`).

post.description: Approve (no apply). pending → approved.
Reject with a required comment. pending → rejected.
Ask the requester to revise (instead of rejecting). pending → needs_revision.

Owner revises and resubmits after a request-changes. needs_revision → pending.

Only the request's owner may resubmit; a foreign id returns 404 (no existence
leak), mirroring the read-path authz.
Apply an approved (or pending, approve+apply shortcut) request via the driver.
Confirm a commit-confirm apply within its window. awaiting_confirm → applied.

schema.title: Response List Audit Api Audit Get

patch.description: Update runtime settings (admin). 422 on an invalid rate-limit string.

AuditEntryOut.title: AuditEntryOut
AuditEntryOut.description: A single audit-log row (also reused by the audit router).

BackupDiffOut.title: BackupDiffOut
BackupDiffOut.description: Unified diff between a stored backup and the current running config.

CredentialsIn.title: CredentialsIn
CredentialsIn.description:
Inbound credential bag. All fields optional; the driver interprets
them per its declared ``auth_methods``. Never echoed back in a response.

DeviceOut.title: DeviceOut
DeviceOut.description: Public view of a device. NEVER includes credentials of any kind.

DeviceWritesIn.title: DeviceWritesIn
DeviceWritesIn.description: Body of ``PATCH /api/devices/{id}/writes`` — the per-device write flag.

DiscoverIn.title: DiscoverIn
DiscoverIn.description: Body of ``POST /api/devices/discover`` — same shape as test-connection.

DriverCapabilities.title: DriverCapabilities
DriverCapabilities.description: What a driver can and cannot do. Surfaced to the UI verbatim.

PortChange.title: PortChange
PortChange.description:
User-facing change request payload.

VLAN IDs are validated against the 802.1Q valid range 1..4094; 0 and 4095
are reserved and rejected at this system boundary.

PortConfigIn.title: PortConfigIn
PortConfigIn.description:
Admin direct edit of on-device port tunables (config write).

All fields optional; at least one must be set. VLAN IDs follow 802.1Q
(1..4094). ``enabled`` maps to the device's admin shut/no-shut.

PortDescriptionIn.title: PortDescriptionIn
PortDescriptionIn.description: Admin direct edit of the port's on-device description (config write).

PortDetailOut.title: PortDetailOut
PortDetailOut.description: Single-port detail: live state + metadata + recent audit history.

PortMetadataPatchIn.title: PortMetadataPatchIn
PortMetadataPatchIn.description: Admin direct edit of port metadata (DB-only; no device write).

PortOut.title: PortOut
PortOut.description: A discovered port, with parsed human fields surfaced for preview.

PortStateOut.title: PortStateOut
PortStateOut.description: A live port plus its human-authored metadata.

ProtocolDetailOut.title: ProtocolDetailOut
ProtocolDetailOut.description: Operational detail for one protocol — named tables from CLI gets.

RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest
RegisterRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /api/auth/register`` (public self-registration).

The role is intentionally absent — self-registered accounts are always
REQUESTER; only an admin can mint privileged users via ``POST /api/users``.
A longer password floor than login applies because this creates the secret.

RequestChangesIn.title: RequestChangesIn
RequestChangesIn.description: Body of ``POST /api/requests/{id}/request-changes`` — what to revise; required.

RequestCreateIn.title: RequestCreateIn
RequestCreateIn.description: Body of ``POST /api/requests`` — file a change request.

RequestL3In.title: RequestL3In
RequestL3In.description: Body of ``POST /api/requests/l3`` — file a routed-interface change.

RequestOut.title: RequestOut
RequestOut.description: Public view of a change request.

RequestResubmitIn.title: RequestResubmitIn
RequestResubmitIn.description:
Body of ``POST /api/requests/{id}/resubmit`` — owner revises and resubmits.

Both fields optional: omit ``requested_changes`` to resubmit unchanged (e.g.
after a back-and-forth in comments), or supply edited changes / reason.

RequestVlanIn.title: RequestVlanIn
RequestVlanIn.description: Body of ``POST /api/requests/vlan`` — file a VLAN-database change.

RequestVrfIn.title: RequestVrfIn
RequestVrfIn.description: Body of ``POST /api/requests/vrf`` — file a VRF create/delete.

write_rate_limit.title: Write Rate Limit
write_rate_limit.description: Write-endpoint rate limit as a slowapi/limits string, e.g. '30/minute'.

SettingsPatch.title: SettingsPatch
SettingsPatch.description: Partial update of runtime settings. Only set fields are applied.

SiteOut.title: SiteOut
SiteOut.description: Public view of a site, with a live device count for the picker.

SiteUpdateIn.title: SiteUpdateIn
SiteUpdateIn.description: Body of ``PATCH /api/sites/{id}`` — rename only (slug is immutable).

SystemInfoOut.title: SystemInfoOut
SystemInfoOut.description: Live system snapshot: device facts, protocols, mgmt services, MAC table.

TestConnectionOut.title: TestConnectionOut
TestConnectionOut.description: Result of a live credential probe. Mirrors the driver TestResult.

UserOut.title: UserOut
UserOut.description: Public view of a user. NEVER includes ``password_hash``.
